title: Add privacy-safe phase diagnostics for Open Library qualification failures
goal: Instrument the trusted TIA V21 Open Library qualification path so a failed migration exposes only a stable operation phase, exception type and HRESULT through the existing public-safe failure field, while raw exception details remain runner-local and qualification/migration semantics remain unchanged.
scope: Primary-maintainer scope: modify only src/TiaV21Worker/Program.cs unless a tiny source-level test file is strictly necessary. Do not modify workflows, generator/domain/compiler semantics, agents, other tasks, runner configuration, secrets, vendor payloads, or IndustrialMDE.

Preserve the exact migration sequence RetrieveWithUpgrade -> Save -> Archive -> current-version Retrieve verification. Do not add fallback APIs, retries, UI/headless changes, or vendor-specific semantic workarounds.
Track stable sanitized phases sufficient to distinguish retrieve-with-upgrade, save, archive, upgrade-close, native-reopen and native-reopen-close failures.

For caught qualification exceptions, expose through QualificationResult.Failure only bounded tokens: stable phase, exception type, and HRESULT rendered in hexadecimal. Do not expose exception Message, stack trace, source/output/work absolute paths, usernames, arbitrary Siemens text, or vendor contents.

Continue storing full Exception.ToString() only in QualificationResult.FailureDetails for runner-local diagnostics. The public qualification workflow must remain unchanged and continue omitting FailureDetails.
Preserve all existing manifest identity/hash/native-reopen/success fields and deterministic identity derivation.

Review the observed run1 process-exit versus manifest discrepancy from trusted run 35430943663. If trusted worker code already returns nonzero for Success=false, do not broaden this candidate into workflow repair; record that the discrepancy is outside this worker-only task.
Candidate/unmerged worker code must never execute on the trusted Windows/TIA runner. Windows/TIA diagnostic validation is post-merge only from trusted main.

requirements: Candidate scope is only src/TiaV21Worker/Program.cs plus an optional strictly bounded source-level test justified by the implementation; no workflow or product/generator files change.
RetrieveWithUpgrade, Save, Archive and native current-version Retrieve execution order and semantics are unchanged.

Upgrade-path caught exceptions produce a public-safe Failure string that identifies the stable phase, exception type and hexadecimal HRESULT without including exception message, stack trace or filesystem paths.
Close failures and native-reopen failures use the same privacy-safe classification discipline.
FailureDetails continues to retain full raw exception information only in the runner-local manifest and is not promoted into public evidence.
Qualification Success remains false on every classified failure and becomes true only after native reopen succeeds exactly as before.
Qualification identity derivation, qualified archive naming, SHA256 handling, existing-archive conflict behavior and deterministic semantics are unchanged.
The candidate does not reinterpret migration failures as BLOCKED; BLOCKED remains a workflow-level timeout/configuration state.

The candidate documents or otherwise makes explicit that Program.RunQualifyLibrary already returns exit code 1 when result.Success is false; no workflow change is included to chase the run1ExitCode observation.
Exact candidate Linux CI is green before merge.

Because primary ChatGPT is expected to materially author this bounded diagnostic candidate, a fresh isolated chatgpt-secondary CODE_REVIEW APPROVE is required for the exact current candidate SHA before merge.
tia: No candidate Windows/TIA execution occurs before independent review and merge.
After merge, rerun /run-olq-001 from issue #19 on trusted main.
A failing trusted run must publish a sanitized failure token that identifies the exact operation phase, exception type and HRESULT while still withholding raw FailureDetails and vendor payloads.

A PASS still requires the unchanged OLQ-001 archive hash/native-reopen/deterministic gates and remains subject to explicit human acceptance before the qualified profile becomes a normal generator dependency.
